claims.claim: Stories must leave the Realms as found: no destroying or irrevocably changing established places, peoples, or gods without dispensation.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: The guide instructs writers and artists to represent the Realms' many skin tones and ethnic analogs, including in cosmopolitan cities.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: Men and women are depicted equally in all roles; sexist clichés (damsel, sexy barmaid) are banned, with orcs and Northlanders as the two exceptions.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: Sex, romance, and gore are kept PG in Realms products.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: In-world characters speak of time loosely ('mid morning', 'nigh sunset') and, where clocks exist, in 'bells', not o'clock.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: Days of the tenday are 'first day', 'second day', and so on; there is no weekend.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: The Realms guide bans a.m./p.m., coffee (kaeth), money (coin), restaurant (feasting hall), week (tenday), hourglass (sandglass), o'clock (bells), and generic subrace names.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: The Realms word list makes 'godsforsaken' the replacement for 'godforsaken'.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: 'Goodsir' is a lowercase form of address; Goodman/Goodwoman are usually capped titles.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)
claims.quote: goodsir (a form of address, not capped)

claims.claim: Common is described as a pidgin trade language, less expressive than regional tongues, which may inform accents.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)
claims.quote: Common is little more than a trade

claims.claim: The guide supplies stock greetings and farewells ('Well met', 'Until swords part') for in-world dialogue.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)
claims.quote: Well met. The most often used greeting

claims.claim: The IP guide tells creators to stay experiential and not use exposition to explain the world.
claims.source: D&D IP Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: Monsters are mostly for killing and looting; non-combat monster roles are exceptions that need explanation.
claims.source: D&D IP Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)
claims.quote: and their stuff is for taking

claims.feature: current AL requirement to follow the D&D Style Guide
claims.claim: The 2025 Dungeoncraft guide (v1.9c) requires the provided template and familiarity with the D&D Style Guide and DMsGuild content guidelines.
claims.source: D&D Adventurers League Dungeoncraft Design Guide v1.9c (effective May 2025, updated 2025-06-23)
claims.quote: You should be familiar with the D&D Style Guide

claims.claim: Dungeoncraft adventures must use the provided template, with an accessible non-template version permitted alongside.
claims.source: D&D Adventurers League Dungeoncraft Design Guide v1.9c (effective May 2025, updated 2025-06-23)
claims.quote: Adventures must use the template provided.
